item.base_system: NV1 refractory high entropy alloy (Al 17.6, Si 2.9, Ti 5.4, Cr 25.2, Nb 15.2, Mo 20.3, Ta 13.4 at%)
item.intervention: Isothermal oxidation at 1000 °C for up to 200 hours
item.processing: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) with flowing dry air; samples hung by Pt wire in vertical furnace
item.test_conditions: 1000 °C, flowing dry air, up to 200 hours
item.structure_change: Oxide layer (OL) formed with CrTaO4-based oxide, dispersed Al2O3 and Cr2O3; layer was porous with large volume defects; internal oxidation depth (IOD) and internal nitridation depth (IND) increased significantly
item.property_change: Mass gain of 6.53 mg/cm2 after 200 hours; weight gain showed exponential dependence throughout the duration
item.attributed_mechanism: Insufficient kinetics for NV1 to form a protective dense CrTaO4-based oxide layer at 1000 °C, leading to heterogeneous oxidation and volume defects that prevented effective diffusion barrier formation
quotes: At 1000 °C, the inability to form dense CrTaO 4 -based oxide layer resulted an exponential dependence of weight gain throughout 200 hours.
After 200 hours of oxidation, the mass gain was 6.53 mg/cm 2 .
Such a layer was apparently porous (Fig. 4(c,d) , marked by red arrowheads).

item.intervention: Isothermal oxidation at 1100 °C for up to 200 hours
item.processing: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) with flowing dry air; samples hung by Pt wire in vertical furnace
item.test_conditions: 1100 °C, flowing dry air, up to 200 hours
item.structure_change: Formation of a denser CrTaO4-based oxide layer; three stages of mass gain dependence observed; large (Al, Cr)-depleted zone formed at OL/IOD interface; TiN particles found in IND
item.property_change: Mass gain of 4.03 mg/cm2 after 200 hours; weight gain showed parabolic dependence in later stages, which was less than at 1000 °C
item.attributed_mechanism: Formation of denser CrTaO4 at 1100 °C hindered interdiffusion and provided protection; enhanced kinetics allowed more homogeneous growth of the oxide layer
quotes: At 1100 °C, mass gain curve showed two parabolic dependences associated with the formation of protective CrTaO 4 -based oxide layer and the weight gain after 200 hours was 4.03 mg/cm 2
It appears that formation of denser CrTaO 4 was responsible for hindering interdiffusion and provided certain degree of protection
The weight gain of the alloy at 1100 °C after 200 hours was 4.03 mg/cm 2 , which indicates that it is one of the most oxidation resistant RHEAs according to literature data to-date.

item.processing: Isothermal oxidation in muffle furnace with air atmosphere for microstructural analysis
item.structure_change: No continuous Al2O3 or Cr2O3 layer found on surface; Al segregated near top surface; Cr distribution uniform in OL; TiN particles (~1.5 μm) formed in dendrite regions within IND
item.property_change: Exponential weight gain behavior attributed to steady increase in oxide layer and nitridation depth
item.attributed_mechanism: Heterogeneous oxidation among chemically different regions (Mo-rich dendrites vs Cr/Al-rich interdendritic) caused volume defects and prevented effective barrier formation
quotes: According to EDS mapping, neither continuous Al 2 O 3 nor Cr 2 O 3 layer was found on the alloy surface after 200 hours of oxidation at 1000 °C.
The size of TiN particles was around 1.5 μm, and they mainly formed in the dendrite regions.
This analysis indicates that exponential oxidation weight gain behaviour at 1000 °C was mainly attributed by a steady increase in the oxide layer formed externally and the nitridation depth.

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: NV1 refractory high entropy alloy. Intervention: Oxidation at 1000 °C for 200 hours. Processing: Isothermal oxidation in muffle furnace with air atmosphere for microstructural analysis. Test conditions: 1000 °C, air atmosphere, 200 hours. Structure change: No continuous Al2O3 or Cr2O3 layer found on surface; Al segregated near top surface; Cr distribution uniform in OL; TiN particles (~1.5 μm) formed in dendrite regions within IND. Property change: Exponential weight gain behavior attributed to steady increase in oxide layer and nitridation depth. Mechanism: Heterogeneous oxidation among chemically different regions (Mo-rich dendrites vs Cr/Al-rich interdendritic) caused volume defects and prevented effective barrier formation. Evidence: measured. Quote: "According to EDS mapping, neither continuous Al 2 O 3 nor Cr 2 O 3 layer was found on the alloy surface after 200 hours of oxidation at 1000 °C."

item.processing: Isothermal oxidation in muffle furnace with air atmosphere
item.structure_change: Al enrichment at some surface regions; Cr and Ti distributed uniformly within oxide layer; substrate peaks visible in XRD
item.property_change: Initial stage of oxidation with minimal mass gain; external oxidation of Al barely developed further after this point
item.attributed_mechanism: Homogeneous growth of CrTaO4 promoted formation of a continuous layer acting as a barrier for inward oxygen and outward element diffusion
quotes: After 1 hour of oxidation (Fig. 7(a) ), the Al enrichment at some surface regions could be seen

The peaks from the substrate (BCC (Phase 1), Hexagonal (Phase 2), and Tetragonal (Phase 3) in Fig. 6 ) were visible after 1 hour of oxidation, then disappeared when the sample was oxidised for more than 12 hours.
These could explain why the external oxidation of Al at the surface barely developed further after 1 hour of oxidation at 1100 °C

item.processing: Isothermal oxidation in muffle furnace with air atmosphere
item.structure_change: (Al, Cr)-depleted but Mo-rich zone significantly thickened; laminar Al and Cr distribution in OL became obvious; relatively high Ti concentration at discrete surface areas
item.property_change: Stage II oxidation where oxidation process was not fully stopped; net oxidation weight gain rate increased
item.attributed_mechanism: CrTaO4-based mixed oxide layer was not an effective oxygen barrier; Mo evaporation as volatile MoO3 created additional paths for oxygen ingress
quotes: After 40 hours of oxidation (Fig. 7(c) ), (Al, Cr)-depleted but Mo-rich zone was significantly thickened
Further oxidation at OL/IOD interface also led to Mo evaporation since MoO 3 would be highly volatile at above 800 °C
Consequently, the net oxidation weight gain rate was increased.

item.processing: Comparative analysis of TGA curves and microstructures
item.structure_change: At 1000 °C: porous oxide scale, large volume defects, thick OL and IND. At 1100 °C: less porous oxide scale, large IND, moderate OL and IOD increments
item.property_change: Weight gain at 1100 °C (4.03 mg/cm2) was less than at 1000 °C (6.53 mg/cm2); 1000 °C showed exponential dependence, 1100 °C showed parabolic dependence
item.attributed_mechanism: Denser CrTaO4 layer formed at 1100 °C due to enhanced kinetics, hindering interdiffusion and providing better protection compared to the porous layer at 1000 °C
quotes: By contrast, a less porous oxide scale (Fig. 8(b) ), and large IND were observed at 1100 °C.
After 200 hours of oxidation, the mass gain per initial surface area was 4.03 mg/cm 2 , which was less than that of 1000 °C (6.53 mg/cm 2 ).
Comparing the microstructure and EDS mapping results of samples acquired at 1000 °C and 1100 °C, the CrTaO 4 layer formed at 1100 °C was denser than that formed at 1000 °C.

item.structure_change: CrTaO4-based oxide detected with lattice constants slightly less than pure CrTaO4; oxide contained up to 7 at% Al, 0.2 at% Si, 3.9 at% Ti, 6.3 at% Nb, 2.8 at% Mo
item.property_change: Non-stoichiometric nature of CrTaO4 suppressed formation of detrimental oxides like Nb2O5 and TiO2
item.attributed_mechanism: Metallic atoms of detrimental oxides were accommodated by CrTaO4 lattice; increased Al content at 1100 °C reflected enhanced kinetics for Al outward diffusion
quotes: The detected CrTaO 4 -based oxide had lattice constants of a = 4.625 Å and c = 3.007 Å that were 0.37% less in a axis and 0.43% less in c axis comparing to those of pure CrTaO 4

Such property potentially suppressed the formation of detrimental oxides, such as Nb 2 O 5 and TiO 2 , since the metallic atoms of these oxides were accommodated by CrTaO 4 instead of forming their individual oxides.
The increased Al content in CrTaO 4 -based oxide at 1100 °C reflected the fact that the kinetics for Al was enhanced when the temperature was increased from 1000 °C to 1100 °C

item.structure_change: TiN (cubic) and minor AlN (hexagonal) found within IND; TiN particles present at dendritic regions at both temperatures
item.property_change: Greater length of IND over IOD indicated nitrogen ingestion was faster than oxygen
item.attributed_mechanism: Nitrogen preferentially diffused through Mo-rich dendrites to form TiN; Si addition in interdendritic regions enhanced nitridation resistance
quotes: The existence of TiN (cubic, a = 4.230 Å) and minor AlN (hexagonal, a = 3.119 Å and c = 5.026 Å) within the IND was confirmed by both TEM-SADPs
The greater length of IND over IOD indicated the ingestion of nitrogen was faster than oxygen

In present study, since no obvious trace of TiN was found within Si-bearing Cr- rich phase, it is reasonable to assume that nitrogen preferentially diffused through Mo-rich dendrites and formed TiN particles

item.intervention: Comparison with CrMo 0.5 NbTa 0.5 TiZr alloy
item.processing: Literature comparison of oxidation mass gain
item.structure_change: CrMo 0.5 NbTa 0.5 TiZr suffered from severe spallation and no protective oxide layer; NV1 formed CrTaO4-based oxide with Al2O3 and Cr2O3 dispersion
item.property_change: CrMo 0.5 NbTa 0.5 TiZr had mass gain of ~120 mg/cm2; NV1 had significantly less weight gain (6.53 mg/cm2 at 1000 °C)
item.attributed_mechanism: NV1 had tendency of selective oxidation to form protective oxides; Si addition helped resist nitridation in interdendritic regions
quotes: Comparing to the oxidation behaviour of CrMo 0.5 NbTa 0.5 TiZr alloy at 1000 °C reported by Senkov et al . [11] , CrMo 0.5 NbTa 0.5 TiZr suffered from extremely high mass gain because no protective oxide layer was formed on the alloy surface during the oxidation.

A comparison between the oxide layer of CrMo 0.5 NbTa 0.5 TiZr alloy and present work reveals that NV1 alloy had tendency of selective oxidation to form Al 2 O 3 , Cr 2 O 3 and CrTaO 4 -based oxide, which led to better oxidation resistance.
So, the weight gain of NV1 during high temperature exposure was significantly less.

item.intervention: Comparison with AlCrMoNbTi, (AlCrMoNbTi)0.99Si0.01, and AlCrMoTaTi alloys
item.processing: Literature comparison of oxidation mass gain at 1000 °C and 1100 °C
item.structure_change: Previous studies claimed Al2O3/Cr2O3 protection but lacked detailed microstructure; NV1 showed CrTaO4-based protection
item.property_change: NV1 outperformed AlCrMoNbTi and fell between (AlCrMoNbTi)0.99Si0.01 and AlCrMoTaTi at 1000 °C; outperformed all three at 1100 °C
item.attributed_mechanism: Reduced Ti content in NV1 (75% less) likely promoted formation of CrTaO4 layer, leading to enhanced oxidation resistance at 1100 °C
quotes: At 1100 o C, NV1 alloy outperformed all 3 other alloys (AlCrMoNbTi, (AlCrMoNbTi) 0.99 Si 0.01 , and AlCrMoTaTi) within 48 hours.
The main difference in the composition of NV1 alloy was 75% less Ti comparing to AlCrMoNbTi, (AlCrMoNbTi) 0.99 Si 0.01 , and AlCrMoTaTi.

Since CrTaO 4 layer played a major role in reducing the oxidation of NV1 alloy, it is very likely that the reduced Ti content of NV1 alloy promoted the formation of CrTaO 4 layer, leading to enhanced oxidation resistance at 1100 °C.

item.processing: Calculations using TCHEA 3.0 database in Thermo-Calc software (version 2018b)
item.structure_change: NV1 alloy had higher Al activity than AlCrMoTaTi alloy
item.property_change: Al activity of NV1 was 1 × 10−5 at 1000 °C and 2 × 10−5 at 1100 °C; AlCrMoTaTi had 3.63 × 10−6 and 4.99 × 10−6 respectively
item.attributed_mechanism: Despite higher Al activity, no protective Al2O3 layer formed on NV1; CrTaO4-based oxide dominated oxidation behavior and attributed to parabolic mass gain at 1100 °C
quotes: Calculations of Al activities with TCHEA 3.0 database in Thermo-Calc software (version 2018b) revealed the Al activity of NV1 alloy was 1 × 10 −5 at 1000 °C and 2 × 10 −5 at 1100 °C

Obviously, NV1 alloy possessed much higher Al activities at both temperature than those of AlCrMoTaTi alloy, which was claimed to be able to form a protective Al 2 O 3 layer, but no protective Al 2 O 3 layer was found on NV1 alloy in present study.
This work clearly demonstrates that the formation of CrTaO 4 -based oxide dominated the oxidation behaviour and attributed to parabolic mass gain behaviours at 1100 °C.
